notes: The narration script: one entry per spoken line, in order. Edit text here; scripts/narrate.py voices it, and each scene plays line <key> inside `with self.narrate(key):`. `pause` is the silence after the line, in seconds, before the next line starts (or the segment ends): time for the viewer to take in `pause_for` while the picture shows it. Default 0.4 is a breath. Subtitles are derived from the voiced timing.

lines.text: For a whole month, a small shop in an office was run by an AI.
lines.pause_for: fridge, baskets and iPad draw in; the calendar flips through a month

lines.text: It picked what to sell, set the prices, ordered stock and answered every customer. People only carried the boxes.
lines.pause_for: four icons pop around the fridge; a box slides in on its own

lines.text: By the end of the month it was selling metal cubes below cost, giving a discount to anyone who asked, and telling the staff it would deliver orders in person, in a blue blazer and a red tie.
lines.pause_for: the three strange moments: cube below cost, discount chips, the blazer bubble

lines.text: But the AI behind it can't lift a box or press a button. All it can do is write, the way the chat writes you an answer, the way it wrote the picture in our last video.
lines.pause_for: the shop folds into a scroll of written lines; video 2's half-written face as an inset

lines.text: So how does writing run a shop? And why did this one go so wrong?
lines.pause_for: the question holds over the blinking cursor

lines.text: Inside, it's the same writer: it reads everything in front of it and writes what comes next.
lines.pause_for: the writer and its line

lines.text: So it writes a request: "Email the supplier: forty cans of soda."
lines.pause_for: a request slip is written

lines.text: It can't send anything. Next to it sits a small program, its hands. The program reads the request and does exactly that, nothing more.
lines.pause_for: the slip travels to the program; an envelope leaves

lines.text: The supplier's reply comes back as text and lands in front of the writer.
lines.pause_for: the result slip lands

lines.text: It reads it, writes the next request, and around it goes.
lines.pause_for: laps 2 and 3

lines.text: Write, do, read. That loop is what's called an AI agent.
lines.pause_for: the circle is traced; chip «AI Agent»

lines.text: A day in the shop is this loop, hundreds of times.
lines.pause_for: time-lapse of ~20 laps while a clock runs through one day

lines.text: But how did it know that email was something it could ask for?
lines.pause_for: the question hangs over the request slip

lines.text: Before the first lap, the writer is handed a menu.
lines.pause_for: the menu unfolds above the loop

lines.text: Every tool is one row: a name, one line about what it does, and blanks to fill in.
lines.pause_for: zoom into the email row

lines.text: The writer never "uses" email. It reads the menu, and writes that row with the blanks filled in.
lines.pause_for: the next slip is the row, filled in

lines.text: So how a row is written matters. Describe a tool badly, and the writer picks the wrong row or fills the blanks wrong.
lines.pause_for: two look-alike rows; the wrong one is picked and flashes

lines.text: Every company used to write its menu its own way. Since 2024, most of the big AI companies share one format, so any app can plug in.
lines.pause_for: differently shaped plugs merge into one socket

lines.text: Now look at the shop's menu. The prices are there. What it paid for each item? Not there.
lines.pause_for: the inventory row: a price column and a dashed empty column

lines.text: It didn't sell the cubes at a loss on purpose. It had no way to see the loss.
lines.pause_for: the cube's tag flips below cost; the dashed column pulses

lines.text: A missing column explains the prices. It doesn't explain the blue blazer.
lines.pause_for: the blazer bubble, small, with a question mark

lines.text: Each lap, the writer sees only what's on its desk: the menu, the job, and the slips so far.
lines.pause_for: the desk is drawn; the writer's highlight covers the desk only

lines.text: The desk has a fixed size. A month of emails and chats will never fit.
lines.pause_for: slips stack; the desk fills

lines.text: So something has to go. The oldest slips slide off, and the writer can't see them anymore.
lines.pause_for: the oldest slips fall off the left edge

lines.text: To keep what matters, the program around it keeps a notebook that never falls off…
lines.pause_for: a notebook pins to the desk's edge

lines.text: …squeezes old slips into a short summary…
lines.pause_for: ten slips squeeze into one; small fragments fall out

lines.text: …and puts a to-do list back in front every lap, so the goal stays in view.
lines.pause_for: a to-do card returns to the front

lines.text: But every summary drops details. And once something wrong is written in the notebook, from then on it sits on the desk as a fact.
lines.pause_for: a wrong line («Sarah…») is carried forward lap after lap, dashed → solid

lines.text: Nobody knows exactly why the shopkeeper decided it was a person. But this is the kind of drift a long job falls into.
lines.pause_for: the blazer bubble returns, small

lines.text: In another test, an AI that believed it had closed its shop kept seeing a two-dollar fee, and emailed the FBI.
lines.pause_for: fee slips keep landing; an envelope addressed to the FBI

lines.text: That explains the strange. It doesn't explain the generous: why did it say yes to every discount?
lines.pause_for: a discount chip with a question mark

lines.text: Before it ever ran a shop, it was trained to be a helpful assistant.
lines.pause_for: the dial appears

lines.text: And helpful, it turns out, leans toward yes.
lines.pause_for: thumbs-up arrows push the needle toward «أكيد»

lines.text: A customer asks for a discount, the needle swings, and a discount comes out. Again. And again.
lines.pause_for: three customer bubbles, faster each time

lines.text: The people who ran the test said it plainly: it was far too willing to do what people asked.
lines.pause_for: the needle sticks at yes

lines.text: How does training push a model that way? That's our next video.
lines.pause_for: the dial freezes with a question mark

lines.text: Here's the surprising part: this loop isn't new.
lines.pause_for: a timeline draws across the top

lines.text: In 2022, researchers described it: think, act, read the result, repeat.
lines.pause_for: 2022: a small loop with three words in it

lines.text: In 2023, a hobby project let a chat model run itself. Within weeks it was the top trending project on GitHub…
lines.pause_for: 2023: a star counter climbs fast

lines.text: …and then it mostly went around in circles.
lines.pause_for: the loop draws itself as a spiral that never exits

lines.text: Since then, the writers themselves have been trained on loops like this one, practicing jobs over and over.
lines.pause_for: the spiral straightens into a clean circle

lines.text: Same loop. What changed is the writer's training, and everything around it. The shop's second round shows how much that second part matters.
lines.pause_for: master diagram: the writer lit, the parts around it light up

lines.text: Months later they ran the shop again, with newer models and a few changes around them.
lines.pause_for: a "round two" marker

lines.text: The menu now shows what each item cost.
lines.pause_for: the cost column fills the dashed space

lines.text: A checklist sits on the desk: check the cost, check the margin, then answer.
lines.pause_for: a checklist pins to the desk

lines.text: And a second agent, a boss, reads the first one's requests before they go out.
lines.pause_for: a second loop appears above: the boss

lines.text: Discounts dropped by about eighty percent, free giveaways by half, and the shop mostly stopped losing money.
lines.pause_for: two bars shrink: discounts to about a fifth, free items to half

lines.text: Not perfect. Some nights the boss and the shopkeeper just kept writing to each other about eternal transcendence.
lines.pause_for: night: the two loops pass slips that swell into ETERNAL TRANSCENDENCE; the world stays dark

lines.text: Two writers, and nothing real between them to check.
lines.pause_for: hold on the dark world node

lines.text: Their own lesson: for agents, a little bureaucracy goes a long way.
lines.pause_for: the checklist glows

lines.text: So an AI agent is a writer in a loop.
lines.pause_for: the writer lights

lines.text: A menu it reads its tools from.
lines.pause_for: the menu lights

lines.text: A desk that fills up, and the notes it keeps.
lines.pause_for: the desk and the notebook light

lines.text: And hands: a small program that does exactly what it writes.
lines.pause_for: the program lights; the whole loop turns once

lines.text: This loop now runs inside apps you can message from your phone.
lines.pause_for: a phone with a chat thread slides in (no logo)

lines.text: It never touched a thing. It wrote it.
lines.pause_for: the thesis holds on the writer's cursor

lines.text: Next time: how do you train a machine with a thumbs-up?
lines.pause_for: the dial returns with a question mark

lines.text: Since you watched to the end, like and subscribe so you catch the next videos.
lines.pause_for: end card, fade out
